Title: Bleeding for 0 (in relation to EC final)

Messages.Author: coincoi...@hotmail.com
Messages.Body:
Hi,

Back to the context
- sunday evening in Goteborg. Five minuts to time limit and Ferenc,
already nearly sure to be European champion, bleeds Olivier with
Yvette, the hopeless (3-cap vampire). Olivier has untapped Aranthebes,
the immortal

"+1 stealth action. Unique. Put this card into play. You may tap
Aranthebes to give a minion controlled by your predator -1 stealth for
the current action. While Aranthebes is untapped, vampires with a
capacity less than 5 get -1 bleed when bleeding you. Any vampire with
a capacity above 4 can move Aranthebes to your library as a (D)
action. Shuffle afterward."

Olivier asks: no block, do you modify?
Ferenc: no, no modifiers
Olivier: so it's a bleed for 0
LSJ then untaps Yvette and say "misplay"

Among the watchers, a lot of questionnings arise between those who
thought that LSJ has lost his nerves and those who were thinking that
the problem had been ruled before.

So, it took me some time to think about it, but I could not find the
ruling about this situation

Question 1: Has this situation previously ruled and if yes, what was
said?

Additional questions I was wondering in case the situation has not
been clarified

[Question 2: Does the fact that Yvette's bleed is a misplay depends on
her potential bleed.
Example: Would Mustafa Rahman who has dominate been treated
differently in the same situation?

Question 3: We are three players left. My prey controls neither
Tremere nor !Tremere. But my predator controls ready Carna, the
princess with and is at 1 pool. If Martin bleeds for 0 and no
reactions/modifiers are played, what happens?

Question 4: Can Samuel Haight bleed for 0, not be blocked, then choose
not to pay 1 blood? What happens next?

"Unique werewolf with 4 life. 3 strength, 0 bleed. Once each action,
Samuel may burn a life to get +1 bleed. He may steal equipment as a
strike. He may play cards requiring basic Celerity [cel] or basic
Thaumaturgy [tha] as a vampire. Any vampire may call a referendum to
make Samuel become Red List as a +1 stealth political action. If
Samuel has less than 4 life during your untap phase, he gains 1 life
from the blood bank."]

Many Thanks

Orian Gissler

Messages.Author: XZealot
Messages.Body:


A minion with a default bleed of zero, may attempt to bleed. Why
would that be a misplay?

Where in the rules does it say that you must have a default bleed of
above zero to attempt to bleed?

Relavent rules.

"6.1.1. Bleed

Bleeding is one of the most fundamental actions of the game. It is the
basic means of removing your prey's pool. By default, your minion's
bleed actions can be directed only at your prey. Some cards or effects
may allow or force you to bleed a Methuselah other than your prey. You
can never bleed yourself, however. A minion cannot perform more than
one bleed action each turn, even if he untaps.

Conceptually, taking a bleed action represents the efforts of your
minion to undermine the power and influence of the target Methuselah.
You might picture bleeding as paying bribes, changing bank records,
spreading rumors, etc.

To bleed a Methuselah, announce the action and tap the acting minion
(the minion who is taking the bleed action). If the action is
successful, the target Methuselah burns an amount of pool equal to the
bleed amount. By default, all minions have a bleed amount of one (most
allies have card text that overrides the default). Additionally, if
the action succeeds and the bleed amount is one or more, then the
bleed is successful and the controller of the acting minion gets the
Edge, taking it from the Methuselah who has it. "

As far as these rules are concerned you can tap and bleed for zero
with 18 Arms Dealers in one turn and if unblocked those actions would
be successful, but since they would be for zero they would not be
successful bleeds.

Comments Welcome,
Norman S. Brown, Jr

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


The declaration was "bleed for 1", not "bleed for 1 minus 1 so it's zero".

The declaration of "bleed for 1" was in error, so the error was corrected (no
action declared).

That is not a mistake in judging. It is proper judging -- correcting erroneous play.

At that point, the player could declare any new action, including a bleed of
zero with that same vampire.

Messages.Author: Johannes Walch
Messages.Body:
LSJ schrieb:


I must agree with LSJ, I was considering a judging error at first but
after I discussed the situation with him it became clear to me.

Correct play is announcing every aspect of the action correctly. So in
that case Ferenc should have announced : "Yvette bleeds for one at zero
stealth". People are used to sloppy play, because they think that it is
faster, but LSJ is really right, announcing the action correctly doesn´t
consume a considerable amount of extra time. Much less in any case than
correcting things afterwards.

Anyway, back to the situation. The action was only rolled back because
the game state was not altered at all between the announcement of the
action and the judgement. If Olivier would have played an On the Qui
Vive, Determine or if a block attempt would have been resolved the game
state would have been changed and I am certain that LSJ would not have
rolled back the game at this point. An error in announcing something
correctly should *not* lead to any advantage of the player.

Also bleeding for 0 would have been a mistake on Ferenc´s side. He was
assuming a bleed for 1 and that is a good action to take at the moment,
so his mistake was not the bleed but the incorrect announcement of the
action (overlooking Aranthebes). We should not punish players for
overlooking one of the 30 cards an Imbued player has on the table, after
all it is a strategy game and not checking every information before
doing something (we all agree that would horrible, I guess).

So the only conclusion I was drawing for myself is that I will be
working hard on my playstyle to announce everything as correct as
possible, and I think others should do the same.

Johannes Walch

Perhaps. That depends on what is judged to be meant by declaring an action with
just the word "bleed" (while tapping minion Bob).

Usually this means "Bob bleeds Bob's prey for 1 at 0 stealth".

So it would be in error, too. Unless the group is used to having Arika with
Repulsion and a Laptop bleed for 4 at 1 stealth being announced as "bleed".

Anyway, it gets less clear when actions aren't properly declared. So, if you
want to make sure you don't get a judgment going against you, the safest bet is
to properly declare your actions.

> Does this mean that when there's a bleed we have to remind the bleeder if
> there is a modifier that reduces the bleed (therefore leaving no place to
> mistake) ?

> discard the card and leave the vampire tapped ; here, in a situation where
> the action was also wrong (not illegal but illegally called) you get a
> rectification instead of a punishment.

Yes. Judging's primary purpose isn't punishment. It's promoting legal play.

When illegal play is made, it is corrected (rectified).

This is the epitome of "fair", not of unfairness.

> Sure, one is illegal play and one
> isn't, but both result from a distraction of the acting player. I understand
> going back in the case of the illegal play, I have trouble considering that
> a simple misplay justifies rewind instead.

All misplays justify corrections. Indeed, they demand correction.

When rewinding is logistically feasible (which is almost always is when the
error is caught when it is announced), then rewinding is usually the best choice
for correction.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <1187767235.1...@e9g2000prf.googlegroups.com>,

Slytherin <an...@operamail.com> writes:
>I have read the rest of this thread, and I am still confused as to why
>the action was illegally declared (regardless of intention or
>mistake).

He declared a bleed for 1, when the bleed was for 0.

Similarly, declaring "Hands for 1" with Quinton McDonnell (+1 strength)
would be misdeclaring your strike, even though he has a base strength of
1. (And so the judge would be entitled to rewind the combat to allow
your opponent to change their strike from, say, strike for hands to a
Dodge.)

>Aranthebes states that a minion has -1 bleed when bleeding you.

And so the bleed was for 0, not for 1.

>This
>surely does not change Yvette's default bleed of 1

It doesn't, but bleed is still for 1.

>and should surely
>be seen as a modifier once the bleed is resolved to be happening
>against Aranthebes controller. If Aranthebes controller redirected the
>bleed, then Yvette would be bleeding for 1, as she is no longer
>bleeding Aranthebes controller.

Right, and you'd declare that to the new target when it was bounced.

> I'm sure this was ruled for vampires
>who have in text +/-1 bleed against a Methuselah who controls a ready
><clan/sect>.

Yes.

>This way declaring Yvette bleeds for 1

Except she's not bleeding for 1. She's bleeding for zero.

If nothing else happens this bleed and it's successful, she'll bleed for
zero. It's that simple.

>I choose not to block, you are therefore bleeding me for 0 with
>Aranthebes modifier

No. Aranthebes does not say "When a bleed is successful, it resolves
for 1 less." It says "vampires... get -1 bleed when bleeding you." So
Yvette was bleeding for zero, right from the start.

>which would be equivalent to
>
>a) I bleed with Yvette for 1
>b) I choose not to block but aus vampire reduces the bleed by 1 with
>Telepathic Counter

Except that Telepathic Counter is a card played during the bleed.
Aranthebes isn't.

Similarly, if Yvette had a laptop computer and no Aranthebes, you
wouldn't say "bleed for 1" and handle the Laptop as an action modifier,
because it isn't.

>In case 1, if it was Ohanna rather than Yvette
>a) Ohanna bleed for 1
>b) I choose not to block, you are therefore bleeding me for 0 with
>Aranthebes modifier

Aranthebes isn't an action modifier and it isn't applied at that point.
It's always been there.

Note that, for example, a weenie vampire who bleeds with base bleed (1)
+ Govern the Unaligned (+2) + Conditioning (+1) would be in range of
Archon Investigation. If they are bleeding a Methuselah who has
Aranthebes, they are bleeding for 3, and so are not in range of Archon
Investigation.

You don't "apply" Aranthebes at some arbitrary point in the action. All
weenie vampires get -1 bleed when bleeding you.



Messages.Author: adam....@gmail.com
Messages.Body:
Similar question but comes up frequently a my playgroup.

Vampire A has inherent bleed of 2.
The Meth A taps said vampire and says "bleed".

The Meth B says "no block, how much"

Meth A states "2" [meaning bleed of 2 no modifiers played]

Upon which Meth B claims that he didn't know that the Vamp had a built
in bleed of 2.
(he would have done the previous if the bleed was for only 1)

Where is the misplay(s)?
What should or shouldn't be taken back?

Adam
Baron of New York

Messages.Author: Jeroen
Messages.Body:
On 24 aug, 15:56, "adam.hu...@gmail.com" <adam.hu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Similar question but comes up frequently a my playgroup.
>
> Vampire A has inherent bleed of 2.
> The Meth A taps said vampire and says "bleed".
>
> The Meth B says "no block, how much"
>
> Meth A states "2" [meaning bleed of 2 no modifiers played]
>
> Upon which Meth B claims that he didn't know that the Vamp had a built
> in bleed of 2.
> (he would have done the previous if the bleed was for only 1)
>
> Where is the misplay(s)?

The misplay is that meth A didn't fully announce his action. He should
have said: 'bleed for 2' (well, if you really want to exagerate:
'vampire A will use the default bleed action targeted at meth B to
bleed for 2 at 0 stealth.')

> What should or shouldn't be taken back?

if possible, the whole action. No-one played any cards in your
example, so that's easy to do.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


I talked on this point back in
http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/msg/319b383f5b208bac

Result: It depends on what was actually communicated by tapping said vampire and
saying "bleed".

Or, rather, on what the judge or arbiter determines/guesses was communicated.

Again, this is why one should properly announce plays.
